actions.justification: Mandatory first step - obtain detailed history including symptom onset, functional status, medication compliance, and precipitating factors for this HFmrEF patient.
Mandatory physical exam to assess for signs of congestion (JVD, peripheral edema, rales), hemodynamic status, and overall clinical profile in this HFmrEF patient.
Mandatory ECG to evaluate for arrhythmias, ischemic changes, conduction abnormalities, or other precipitants of heart failure decompensation.
Mandatory lab to assess renal function, electrolytes, and glucose in a patient with HFmrEF; essential for guiding therapy and detecting contraindications.
Mandatory biomarker for heart failure diagnosis, severity assessment, and prognosis in this patient with known HFmrEF (EF 41-49%).
Mandatory imaging to evaluate for pulmonary congestion, cardiomegaly, and other cardiopulmonary pathology in this heart failure patient.
Mandatory action - CBC to evaluate for anemia (common HFmrEF exacerbating factor) and baseline hematologic status within 60-minute deadline.
Mandatory action - TSH to rule out thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism/hyperthyroidism) as a contributing cause or exacerbating factor for heart failure with mildly reduced EF (41-49%).
Assess hemodynamic profile (warm/cold, wet/dry) to guide further management decisions including diuretic therapy and vasodilator use in this HFmrEF patient.

With HFmrEF and EF 41-49%, assessment for ICD implantation is indicated per heart failure guidelines to evaluate for sudden cardiac death prevention.
Evaluate for cardiac resynchronization therapy candidacy given HFmrEF diagnosis, which may improve symptoms and outcomes if QRS prolongation or LBBB is present.

Patient has HFmrEF (EF 41-49%). NYHA functional class assessment is essential to guide therapy decisions including beta-blocker, ACE inhibitor/ARB, and other guideline-directed medical therapy titration.
Assessing structural abnormalities (e.g., valvular disease, LV remodeling) is important in HFmrEF to identify reversible or treatable causes and guide management.

Cardiac rehabilitation is a guideline-recommended intervention for heart failure patients to improve functional capacity, quality of life, and outcomes, and should be assessed/initiated when appropriate.

Patient has HFmrEF (EF 41-49%) and requires assessment of guideline-directed medical therapy optimization. Checking GDMT status is essential next step to guide pharmacological management in heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction.

With HFmrEF and EF 41-49%, assessing candidacy for advanced therapies (ICD, CRT, or other device therapy) is appropriate after initial workup to determine if the patient meets criteria for escalation of care.
HR is 80 bpm. Ivabradine may be indicated if patient remains in sinus rhythm with HR ≥70 bpm on maximally tolerated beta-blocker therapy per ACC/AHA HF guidelines for HFrEF/HFmrEF patients.

Patient has HFmrEF (EF 41-49%). After comprehensive workup, confirming optimal GDMT (guideline-directed medical therapy) status is essential to ensure appropriate therapy including ACE inhibitor/ARB/ARNI, beta-blocker, and MRA are being maximized.
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) are recommended for HFmrEF to reduce morbidity and mortality. Assess whether this patient is on appropriate renin-angiotensin system blockade.

Beta-blockers are recommended in HFmrEF patients to reduce hospitalization and mortality. With stable vitals (HR 80, BP 120/80), patient appears hemodynamically stable and may tolerate initiation or optimization of beta-blocker therapy.

Patient has HFmrEF (EF 41-49%) and is on GDMT. Adding a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (e.g., spironolactone/eplerenone) is recommended per guidelines for heart failure to reduce morbidity and mortality, provided renal function and potassium are acceptable (awaiting BMP results).
Assess for volume overload/congestion in this HFmrEF patient. Diuretic therapy is indicated if signs of fluid retention are present to relieve symptoms and improve hemodynamics.

Although currently hemodynamically stable (BP 120/80, HR 80), patient has HFmrEF with EF 41-49%. Evaluate whether low-dose inotropic support may be needed based on clinical trajectory and pending labs (CBC, BMP).
